verses.verse:
वार्तालापस्तु भाषायाम् विलापो रोदने भवेत्।
संलापोऽभिनयादौ स्यात्तथाऽलापः स्वरेषु च।११२।
verses.text: Vārtālāpa (conversation) belongs to language; vilāpa (lament) is in weeping; saṃlāpa (dialogue) is in acting and the like; and likewise ālāpa is in notes.

commentary.text: Bhāva (feeling) has existed ever since this world was created. Or say that creation itself is full of bhāva, and pralaya (dissolution) is its absence (abhāva). It became necessary for living beings to exchange feelings with one another. It is from just there that we must take the various languages and gestures to have arisen. Along with languages, nāda (sound), and along with gestures, laya (rhythm) arose naturally. When one being began to wish to nurture another, from then on lāpana (speaking) also became necessary. According to the grammar of Śrī Pāṇini, from the root pal comes lāp or pālana (nurturing), and from the root lap comes lāp or lāpana (speaking); these two roots became each other's avaroha (reversal). In the śloka above, the meanings of the root lap with prefixes, and their fields, are shown. If vārtālāpa (conversation) is suited to language, then in the same way vilāpa (lament) is suited to weeping, saṃlāpa (dialogue) to acting, and in the same way ālāpa to notes.
